sections.html:
Greece is Monroe County's most populous town and wraps around Rochester's northwest corner. Houses run from Ridge Road in the south to the Lake Ontario shoreline. The 2025 population of 94,484 sits below the 96,926 counted in 2020, so demand isn't being pushed up by new arrivals. Owners live in 72.7% of the homes. Values center on $190,300, median rent is $1,170, and workers spend 20.5 minutes getting to their jobs, a detail that tends to appeal to buyers relocating from elsewhere.

Braddock Bay and other wetlands and ponds sit along the northern edge. New York's disclosure form has questions on wetlands and flood zones, so go slowly over those lines if your lot is close to the water.

Three districts split the town: Greece Central, Hilton Central and Spencerport Central. ZIP code 14468 is Hilton and 14559 is Spencerport, which means a mailing address can point to a different district than you expect. Spell out the district whenever you describe the house to anyone.

sections.h2: Town rules that can slow a sale
sections.html:
On a Greece house, two problems stall closings more than any others: permits that were never finished and code violations visible from the street. The Building Department sits within Technical Services at One Vince Tofany Boulevard. A remodel or addition to a single-family house needs a permit, and once the work costs more than $20,000 the plans must be professionally prepared.

  • A permitted project passes through footing and foundation, rough framing, insulation and final grading checks. An electrical sign-off comes from one of three listed inspection agencies, and the town does a last inspection at the end.
  • The town's property maintenance law reaches vacant buildings and empty land too. The penalty is as much as $1,000 or a year in jail for each violation, and the town can make the repair itself and send you the cost on your tax statement.
  • Trash pickup has to be active at every home. Vehicles that are dismantled or unlicensed can't be left in the yard.
  • Keep your for sale sign to one, no bigger than six square feet, and off the roadside right of way and utility poles.

Rental applications, both short-term and long-term, are posted beside the building forms. Look at them if tenants will stay after the sale. And before any contract is signed, have the department confirm that earlier work was closed out.

Each January the Receiver of Taxes collects the town's general taxes for the calendar year. The mailing in early January combines the Town, Monroe County, the Greece Fire District, the Greece Central School District and any special districts. A school or water charge left unpaid gets re-levied onto that same bill, so ask the closing attorney to check whether one is waiting.

Rates for the county, fire district and schools aren't the town's to set. Town Hall just collects. You can pay in person on weekdays or leave a payment in the 24 hour drop at the Service Mall entrance. Online payments run through Monroe County's website with a 3 percent charge on cards. Phone payments aren't taken.

Take your latest bill to the attorney. The other side will ask for a printout of paid and open amounts on the parcel, and the Receiver's office can supply it.

There are three stages. The first is free and happens early in the year. Because a lower assessment also helps whoever buys next, winning before you list can back up your asking price.

  • Informal hearing: by appointment with the Assessor's Office, from January to March.
  • Board of Assessment Review: file form RP-524 after May 1 and by the fourth Tuesday of May, and request either a hearing or a review of the papers.
  • Judicial review: when the board's result still seems wrong, form RPTL-730 and fees must be filed within 30 days after the final roll is published.

The town assesses as of March 1 and uses the July 1 before that as its valuation day, so work finished after March 1 shows up on the next roll. A spring sale can overlap with an appeal that hasn't been decided. Tell the buyer if so.

sections.h2: What recording a deed costs in Monroe County
sections.html:
The Monroe County Clerk records Greece deeds at 39 West Main Street in Rochester, and same-day recording means standing in line by 4:30 p.m. The clerk's land records page shows the going charges.

Monroe County recording charges for a residential deed
Recording chargeAmount
One page deed$50, plus $5 for each added page
TP-584 form$5
Equalization form RP-5217$125 for common residential cases, otherwise $250
Transfer tax$4 per thousand dollars of price
Residential deed add-on$10 per deed

Most sellers never visit the counter, because the attorney or title company files the deed and tallies every charge ahead of closing.

Once you and the buyer settle on a price, the two attorneys exchange a contract while the buyer orders a title search. Anything it uncovers, such as unpaid school or water bills, open permits or liens, is paid off or credited at the table. Real Property Law section 462 also requires you to hand over a signed property condition disclosure statement before the contract is signed.

The closing itself is mostly signing: the deed, the transfer forms and the payoff to your lender, which comes straight out of your proceeds. Then the deed goes to the county clerk. Buyers paying cash for a house as is can often close sooner, since there's no loan approval or appraisal in the way. Clear title still matters, and so does a closing date you've agreed to in writing.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before offers arrive
sections.html:
• The signed disclosure statement.
  • Permit records for each finished basement, deck, pool or addition.
  • A current tax bill showing every taxing line.
  • A payoff figure from your lender, plus any liens.
  • Keys, access and the closing date you want.

Selling for cash gets rid of showings, appraisals and an inspector's repair list. The paperwork above still applies. Pull it together now and any route to closing goes faster, whether you list or take a direct offer.

Look at the amount that reaches your account, not the headline price. A listing may show a bigger number, but commission, repairs and carrying costs come out of it. A direct buyer's lower figure may leave you even if it closes quickly and asks for no fix-up work. Request each offer in writing with the closing date and proof of funds, and settle who pays the transfer tax and recording charges before you sign.

faqs.q: Is Greece, NY part of Rochester?
faqs.a: No. Greece is its own town in Monroe County, with the city of Rochester on its eastern border. Taxes come from the Town of Greece, the county and the fire district, and the schools are Greece Central, Hilton Central or Spencerport Central.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit record to sell a Greece house?
faqs.a: Selling doesn't call for a permit. Still, open building permits and exterior code violations can stall a closing, so ask the Building Department to confirm that earlier work was closed out.

faqs.q: When do Greece town and county taxes get billed?
faqs.a: The bill is mailed in early January for the year from January 1 through December 31. The Receiver of Taxes collects it, and any unpaid school or water charge is added to it.

faqs.q: How much is the Monroe County transfer tax on a deed?
faqs.a: It is $4 per thousand dollars of the sale price, plus the recording and form fees. Your attorney can give you the exact total before closing.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to grieve a Greece assessment?
faqs.a: File form RP-524 after May 1 and by the fourth Tuesday of May. The Assessor holds informal hearings earlier, from January to March.
